description: PermianMAP, the Permian Methane Analysis Project, is an Environmental Defense Fund project with Scientific Aviation and university researchers that combined satellites, helicopters, aircraft, vehicles and towers to pinpoint, measure and report oil and gas methane emissions in the Permian Basin, the largest oil field on the planet across about 86,000 square miles of West Texas and southeastern New Mexico. The page hosts an interactive map, findings and a final summary report. Reported findings include ground and aerial surveys showing methane escaping at about three times the national average, low-producing marginal wells responsible for half of well pad emissions, and a flare survey finding that at least one in ten surveyed flares was unlit or burning inefficiently; satellite data from TROPOMI published in Science Advances rank the basin as the highest-emitting in the United States. Access: the public website and its map; no bulk download or licence is stated on the page. Caveats: an advocacy organisation's project with data shown as maps and summaries, and no data download is shown on the page. It suits methane leak and flaring exposure analysis and gas system loss modelling, and relates to the EIA petroleum supply and prices record catalogued here.
